headline: Computational guide RNA design accounting for population variants and viral diversity
label: Computational Sequence Design Tools
summary: Population variants are shown to alter CRISPR guide on-target activity, motivating haplotype-aware sequence design.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational design of nucleotide sequences under explicit constraints, with candidate guides assessed computationally. CRISPR-HAWK treats population variation and haplotype structure as design inputs, reporting that variants alter guide on-target activity across 79,648 genomes. The Dengue study designs PspCas13b guide RNAs intended to be conserved across all four serotypes and benchmarks Random Forest and XGBoost models against RNA-FM. What is new is that population sequence diversity and viral serotype conservation are treated as explicit design objectives. The PfEMP1 functional-systems paper does not perform sequence design and is included for context only, so the shared thread is methodological rather than a single application.
